text: It looked like a good idea. <break time="0.8s" /> But wait until I tell you. <break time="0.8s" /> What happened. <break time="0.8s" /> Bill Driscoll and I. <break time="0.8s" /> Were down South in Alabama. <break time="0.8s" /> When this kidnapping idea came to us. <break time="0.8s" /> We had about six hundred dollars. <break time="0.8s" /> But we needed two thousand more. <break time="0.8s" /> For a dishonest land plan. <break time="0.8s" /> In Summit. <break time="0.8s" /> A town as flat as a pancake. <break time="0.8s" /> We chose the only son. <break time="0.8s" /> Of a rich man named Ebenezer Dorset. <break time="0.8s" /> The boy was ten years old. <break time="0.8s" /> With lots of freckles. <break time="0.8s" /> And bright red hair. <break time="0.8s" /> About two miles from Summit. <break time="0.8s" /> There was a small mountain. <break time="0.8s" /> Covered with thick cedar trees. <break time="0.8s" /> On the far side of the mountain. <break time="0.8s" /> Was a cave. <break time="0.8s" /> And we stored our food there. <break time="0.8s" /> One evening. <break time="0.8s" /> We drove a buggy. <break time="0.8s" /> Past old Dorsets house. <break time="0.8s" /> And found the boy. <break time="0.8s" /> Throwing stones at a kitten. <break time="0.8s" /> When Bill offered him. <break time="0.8s" /> Candy and a nice ride. <break time="0.8s" /> The boy hit him in the eye. <break time="0.8s" /> With a brick. <break time="0.8s" /> That will cost the old man. <break time="0.8s" /> An extra five hundred dollars. <break time="0.8s" /> Said Bill. <break time="0.8s" /> Climbing over the wheel. <break time="0.8s" /> The boy fought like a little bear. <break time="0.8s" /> But at last. <break time="0.8s" /> We got him into the buggy. <break time="0.8s" /> And drove away.
